title: Explicit multiplicative functions
summary: The numerically explicit layer of multiplicative number theory on Mathlib's ArithmeticFunction carrier: explicit bounds for the summatory functions M, m, m̌ of the Möbius function (with semigroup restrictions and character twists) and the general conversion theorems behind them (Meissel–MacLeod–Balazard identities, Balazard's conversion, Ramaré's prime-to-Möbius transfer with every finite computation named), the convolution comparison theorem with its models, explicit upper bounds for averages of nonnegative multiplicative functions, the explicit averages of μ², μ²/φ, τ, τ_k, τ², 2^ω, φ, the explicit Mertens and tilted Euler products, and the pointwise bounds for ω, τ_k, σ, σ*; every analytic input is a parameter or a named Prop and every published constant is an instance; brought to the current explicit record: Ramaré–Zuniga Alterman's |M(X)| ≤ (0.006688 log X − 0.039)X/log²X, the linear bounds from finitely many zeros of ζ under a named residue-sum hypothesis, Daval's conversions, Johnston–Leong–Tudzi's x/(log x)^k iteration, the comparison theorem for a general exponent with the Platt–Trudgian model, the squarefree remainder from zeros, the Piltz remainders Δ_k, Axler's cubic Mertens product and the pointwise bounds for σ(n)/n and n/φ(n); preprints are cited and the refereed statements are kept alongside.
